transcript.text: We had a power cut last night and now our Candy washer dryer is completely dead - no lights, nothing. Everything else in the house came back on. The plug fuse is fine, I swapped it. Help!

A sound plug fuse rules out one simple cause, but it does not prove the washer-dryer’s wall socket is live. With the washer-dryer unplugged, test that exact socket using a known-good low-power item such as a phone charger, and check the socket switch is on. If the socket is dead, check the relevant breaker/RCD at the consumer unit or use an electrician; do not keep trying the washer-dryer. If the socket works but the Candy remains completely dead, the power cut may have damaged its mains filter, internal wiring or control board, which needs an appliance engineer rather than opening it up.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
I've already tested that socket with a lamp and it works fine. I also unplugged the washer-dryer for over 10 minutes and tried again, still dead. The consumer unit has everything switched on too.

Sound plug fuse and no recovery after being unplugged, this is very likely an internal power-supply fault rather than a setting or reset issue. The leading possibilities are the mains suppressor/filter or its connections, followed by the power-supply section of the main control board; a power cut or surge can expose either fault. As it is completely dead, keep it unplugged and arrange an appliance engineer—this needs internal mains-voltage diagnosis and should not be opened by a homeowner. If there is any burning smell, heat at the plug or cable, or visible damage, do not reconnect it at all.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.

candidates: Loss of supply at the washer-dryer socket or switched spur (medium)
Surge-damaged mains filter, wiring or control board (medium)

The fault they reported is: "completely dead, no lights or power after a power cut". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 2: the checks they reported did not fix it. Give the next check that best separates the remaining likely causes, or say what the likely faulty part is if the checks already point to one. Until a check has confirmed which part has failed, name it as the likely part and the check that would confirm it; do not tell them to buy, order or replace it.
